doc.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

title: Cannonball's horns and hearing versus practicing changes
summary: His King Super 20 then Selmer, and how Cannonball heard rather than practiced changes.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: You know I noticed a slight difference when he used to play, he used to play a King I think, right?
And then he switched to Selmer. I could tell.
He loved that King Super 20. That’s what he had. He had a Super 20, he loved that. Then he played the Selmer. That’s right.
I think he got an endorsement or something like that.

But that didn’t make no difference because he was going to get it — he could have got the cheapest horn in the world, he was going to get what he heard to get out of it. And as far as changes, believe me, that didn’t mean nothing. I mean the cat sat down, he’s spelling changes and going oh man look, Cannonball, he heard all of that. He just went on through that.
Oh yeah he knew them. But he could hear them. He could hear that. He didn’t have to sit down and practice them like them cats do that.
